details: Bitcoin experienced a sharp drop to approximately $77,614 following reports of potential US and Israeli military strikes against Iran. This escalation of geopolitical tension triggered a significant sell-off in risky assets, including cryptocurrencies, wiping out over $40 billion from the crypto market capitalization and leading to substantial liquidations in derivative markets. The concurrent rise in oil prices also fueled inflation fears, further contributing to overall market instability.
title: US-Israel-Iran Tensions Cause Bitcoin Plunge, $40B Market Cap Lost

details: Bitcoin and the broader cryptocurrency market are facing increased pressure from macroeconomic factors, including surging US bond yields and higher-than-expected inflation reports. This shift has led market participants to anticipate either prolonged pauses in interest rate cuts or even potential rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, making non-yielding assets like Bitcoin less attractive to investors and fostering a risk-off sentiment in global financial markets.
title: Rising Bond Yields & Inflation Fears Weigh on Bitcoin Market

details: Following recent high-level talks, the United States and China have reached a tentative agreement to reduce tariffs and ease non-tariff barriers, particularly concerning agricultural products and certain other goods. This development aims to boost bilateral trade and could positively influence global risk sentiment, potentially encouraging capital flows towards riskier assets, including cryptocurrencies.
title: US and China Tentatively Agree to Reduce Tariffs, Easing Trade Tensions

details: Russian President Vladimir Putin is scheduled to undertake a state visit to China from May 19-20. This significant diplomatic event, occurring shortly after recent US-China discussions, is expected to have notable implications for global trade, energy markets, geopolitical alliances, and international economic strategy as both nations look to deepen their strategic partnership.
title: Putin to Visit China Amid Rising Geopolitical Tensions, Strengthening Ties
